rules:
- id: vuln-notesnook-e87f5e5f
  patterns:
    - pattern: |
        const $ANCHOR = document.createElement("a");
        $ANCHOR.href = $SRC;
        ...
        $ANCHOR.outerHTML
    - pattern-not: |
        const $ANCHOR = document.createElement("a");
        $ANCHOR.href = `${$SRC}?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw`;
        ...
        $ANCHOR.outerHTML
  message: "Potential XSS vulnerability due to unescaped user input in anchor href attribute. The src value is directly inserted into the href without proper sanitization, which could allow attackers to inject malicious URLs or JavaScript code. Fix by properly escaping or validating the src input before constructing the href."
  severity: ERROR
  languages: [typescript]
  metadata:
    source-url: "github.com/streetwriters/notesnook/commit/e87f5e5f899f45df28d7c0f33f15e9178d1fbcb7"
    category: security
    cwe: [79]

Analyze the following vulnerability patch and generate a precise Semgrep rule to detect similar vulnerabilities in typescript code. CONTEXT: Repository: github.com/streetwriters/notesnook Commit: e87f5e5f899f45df28d7c0f33f15e9178d1fbcb7 PATCH CHANGES: File: packages/editor/src/extensions/embed/component.tsx --- a/packages/editor/src/extensions/embed/component.tsx +++ b/packages/editor/src/extensions/embed/component.tsx + + const anchor = document.createElement("a"); + anchor.href = `${src}?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw`; + - }>

`; + }>

${ + anchor.outerHTML + }

`; UNDERSTAND THE MECHANISM FIRST: Before writing a rule, identify the underlying vulnerability MECHANISM the patch fixes -- the specific unsafe condition (e.g. untrusted data reaching a dangerous sink without a check, a missing bounds/escaping/validation step, an unsafe default). Do not simply pattern-match the exact expression shown in the diff: the same vulnerable mechanism will also appear, in the held-out test variants, with renamed identifiers AND with the vulnerable logic moved into a different function or otherwise restructured (e.g. extracted into a small helper, inlined, or reordered). Write the rule to catch the mechanism wherever it appears in the file, not only at this exact call site or inside this exact function. SEMGREP PATTERN SYNTAX GUIDE: - Use $VARNAME to match any expression - Use ... to match any sequence of statements - Use pattern-inside to limit matches to specific code blocks - Use pattern-not to exclude specific patterns (like the fixed version) - Use metavariable-pattern to add constraints on variables - A single `pattern` is only one option. Where the vulnerable mechanism can show up in more than one syntactic shape (e.g. the same unsafe call reachable through a helper function, or several equivalent call forms), prefer `patterns`/`pattern-either` to cover them together, rather than only the one shape seen in this diff. - `patterns` (a list under one `pattern`-family key) means EVERY listed pattern must match the SAME code location -- it is for combining different CONDITIONS on one spot (e.g. a call plus a pattern-not exclusion), not for joining two separate statements that merely both need to be present. Two or more statements that occur together in sequence belong in ONE multi-line `pattern:` block (write them one after another, exactly like plain code), not as separate entries under `patterns`. - For a mechanism that is really about untrusted data reaching a dangerous sink, consider a taint-mode rule instead: `mode: taint` with `pattern-sources` (where the untrusted data enters) and `pattern-sinks` (the dangerous use) -- this generalizes across refactors that a single structural pattern cannot, since it tracks the data, not the exact code shape. REQUIRED FIELDS: 1. id: "vuln-notesnook-e87f5e5f" (must be unique and descriptive) 2. At least one of: pattern, patterns, pattern-either, pattern-regex, or (mode: taint with) pattern-sources and pattern-sinks 3. languages: ["typescript"] 4. message: Detailed description of what the vulnerability is, why it's dangerous, how to fix it 5. severity: One of [ERROR, WARNING, INFO] RECOMMENDED FIELDS: - pattern-not: Pattern that should not match (e.g., fixed version) - pattern-inside / pattern-not-inside: Context pattern for where the rule should/should not match - metadata: source-url: github.com/streetwriters/notesnook/commit/e87f5e5f899f45df28d7c0f33f15e9178d1fbcb7 category: security cwe: [relevant CWE number] IMPORTANT GUIDELINES: 1. Make patterns as specific as possible to minimize false positives on the patched/safe code 2. Include pattern-not for the fixed version when possible 3. Consider that the vulnerable mechanism may be reached through a renamed or restructured call site, not only the exact one shown in the diff 4. Write clear, actionable messages explaining both the problem and solution EXAMPLES OF HIGH-QUALITY RULES: FORMAT YOUR RESPONSE AS A SINGLE YAML DOCUMENT with exactly one rule under `rules:`. Do not include Markdown fences or prose before or after it.
